name: The Content Engine: Solo Founder Edition
tagline: Turn a single core idea into an entire week of targeted social media posts in minutes.
metaDescription: Discover 12 plug-and-play prompts designed for solo founders to repurpose one core idea into a full week of high-converting content across platforms.
description:
As a solo founder, your biggest bottleneck isn't building your product—it's marketing it consistently without burning out. You have great ideas, but sitting down to write separate posts for X, LinkedIn, and your newsletter takes hours you don't have.

**The Content Engine** solves this by giving you a systematic, 12-prompt framework to atomize a single core concept into a week's worth of multi-platform content. 

### Who It's For
Bootstrapped founders, indie hackers, and solo entrepreneurs who need to maintain a consistent social media presence to drive organic growth without a dedicated marketing team.

### What Problem It Solves
It eliminates blank-page syndrome and the fatigue of daily brainstorming. Instead of wondering what to post, you feed your latest milestone, customer insight, or product update into these prompts to instantly generate tailored copy.

### Why These Prompts Work
These aren't generic writing prompts. They are engineered using advanced copywriting frameworks (like PAS, AIDA, and story-driven arcs) specifically tuned for the B2B and indie SaaS landscapes. Each prompt includes a specific usage tip to help you inject your authentic founder voice, ensure high engagement, and drive traffic back to your landing page.
includes: 1 Notion template containing all 12 production-ready prompts
Markdown (.md) file for easy copy-pasting into ChatGPT or Claude
3 distinct categories: Thread & Short-form, Long-form & Authority, and Newsletter & Email
sampleItems: Act as a direct response copywriter. Take my core idea about bootstrapping and rewrite it into a 5-tweet thread using the Hook-Story-Offer framework.
Act as a B2B content strategist. Convert my latest product update into a professional, insight-driven LinkedIn post that appeals to busy executives.

items.title: The 5-Tweet Narrative Thread
items.body: Act as an expert growth marketer. Take my core idea below and break it down into a 5-part Twitter/X thread. Tweet 1 must be a high-curiosity hook under 280 characters without using clickbait clichés. Tweets 2 through 4 should deliver rapid-fire value, breaking the concept into actionable lessons. Tweet 5 must end with a clear, low-friction call-to-action inviting engagement or a newsletter sign-up. Usage tip: Replace any abstract jargon with concrete numbers or timeframe metrics from your actual founder journey before posting.

items.title: The Contrarian Authority Post
items.body: Act as a contrarian industry analyst. Take my core idea and formulate a LinkedIn post that challenges conventional wisdom in my niche. Start with a bold, polarizing opening statement that stops the scroll. Follow up with three logical arguments supported by common founder mistakes, and conclude with a forward-looking prediction. Keep paragraphs short—one to two sentences max—to maximize mobile readability. Usage tip: Ensure your stance is genuinely held; mild controversy builds authority, but fake outrage damages trust.

items.title: The Behind-The-Scenes Builder Story
items.body: Act as a narrative essayist. Translate my core idea into a vulnerable, behind-the-scenes founder story. Focus on a specific challenge, mistake, or breakthrough moment I experienced while working on my startup. Structure the post using a narrative arc: the inciting struggle, the turning point realization, and the ultimate takeaway for other builders. Usage tip: Avoid toxic positivity; acknowledging a real failure makes your eventual success far more compelling to potential users.

items.title: The Step-by-Step Tactical Playbook
items.body: Act as a technical documentation writer turned marketer. Convert my core idea into a chronological, step-by-step tutorial post for indie hackers. Format the output with clear numbered steps (1 through 5), including specific tools, metrics, or methods used at each stage. End with a prompt asking readers which step they struggle with the most. Usage tip: Use this prompt when you have recently solved a frustrating technical or operational problem in your business.

items.title: The Customer Problem-Agitation-Solution (PAS)
items.body: Act as a direct-response conversion copywriter. Take my core idea and adapt it into a short-form promotional post using the PAS (Problem-Agitate-Solution) framework. First, vividly describe the pain point my target user feels daily. Second, agitate that pain by highlighting the hidden costs of inaction (lost time, wasted money, stress). Third, introduce my product as the effortless, elegant solution. Usage tip: Keep the transition to your product seamless so the post reads like helpful advice rather than a desperate sales pitch.

items.title: The Data-Driven Insight Breakdown
items.body: Act as a startup data analyst. Transform my core idea into an analytical post that highlights a surprising trend, metric, or user behavior observation. Present the data point immediately in the hook, explain the 'why' behind the numbers in the body, and offer a strategic recommendation for solo founders trying to scale. Usage tip: If you don't have public metrics, use internal beta-test observations or anonymized user feedback to back up your claims.

items.title: The Quick-Hit Bulleted Takeaways
items.body: Act as a busy curator. Distill my core idea into a punchy, ultra-scannable listicle optimized for LinkedIn or X. Provide an introductory sentence, followed by 5 distinct bullet points beginning with strong action verbs, and wrap up with a summary question that drives comments. Usage tip: This is your go-to format when you are short on time but still want to ship daily content to maintain algorithmic momentum.

items.title: The Founder FAQ & Objection Crusher
items.body: Act as a skeptical customer success lead. Take my core idea and frame it as an answer to the most common objection prospective users have about my product or niche. Start by stating the objection bluntly ('Why bother building in public when...'), dismantle it with logic and personal experience, and position your product as the natural answer. Usage tip: Pull this objection directly from a recent customer email, DM, or Reddit comment you received.

items.title: The Weekly Newsletter Deep Dive
items.body: Act as an expert email newsletter editor. Expand my core idea into a 400-word standalone newsletter issue. Include a catchy subject line, a personal opening anecdote, a comprehensive exploration of the core idea, three actionable takeaways, and a soft promotional mention of my product at the very bottom. Usage tip: Send this out on Tuesday or Thursday mornings when B2B open rates peak for solo operators and decision-makers.

items.title: The Visionary Future-Of-The-Industry Post
items.body: Act as a startup futurist. Take my core idea and project it five years into the future of my industry. Write a visionary post detailing how current trends will transform the landscape, what legacy tools will die out, and how solo founders can position themselves to win. Usage tip: Bold predictions generate massive shares and attract high-value networking opportunities with other forward-thinking founders.

items.title: The Interactive Poll & Discussion Starter
items.body: Act as a community manager. Convert my core idea into a high-engagement post designed to spark debate and gather qualitative market research. Frame the post around a common industry dilemma, present two contrasting paths forward, and invite the audience to vote or explain their reasoning in the comments. Usage tip: Read every comment reply and use the insights to generate ideas for your next three pieces of content.

items.title: The Milestone & Lessons Learned Retrospective
items.body: Act as a reflective solo founder documenting the journey. Take my core idea and turn it into a milestone celebration post that avoids humble-bragging by focusing entirely on the painful lessons learned along the way. Detail what went wrong, what you changed, and what advice you would give to someone starting out today. Usage tip: Authenticity wins online; sharing a specific mistake you made builds vastly more rapport than just posting a revenue screenshot.
